header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue #81 in AlexITC/expense-tracker: make pages URL friendly so selected filters live in the URL, starting with the bank statements account/status filter, and document the pattern. Full spec follows.

## Problem

Page state that the user selects is not reflected in the URL, so pages are not refreshable or shareable, and navigating back loses context.

Concrete case on the bank statements page (`web/.../pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsPage.scala`): selecting an account (the account filter) lives only in component state. Refreshing the page loses the selection, and going from a statement review back to the list does not restore the account that was selected. It resets to the default.

## Goal

Make selected filters and view state live in the URL.

- Selecting a bank statement account updates the URL (query param, e.g. `?account=<key>`), so a refresh restores the same account and the URL is shareable.
- Returning from a statement review to the list keeps the same account selected. The back navigation lands on the list with its prior filter intact.
- Deep links resolve on a cold load (this overlaps with the ctrl+click bug in #80, where opening `/bank-statements/{id}` in a new tab lands on the default page instead of the statement).

## Pattern to document

This is a general rule, not a one-off. Add it to the frontend guide (`docs/guide/frontend.md`): **pages must be URL friendly. User-selected filters and view selections go in the URL (path or query params), not only in component state, so pages are refreshable, shareable, and back-navigable.** Read initial state from the URL on mount; write to the URL on change (replace vs push chosen so the browser back button behaves sensibly).

## Scope

- Phase 1: the bank statements account filter, plus any other filters already on that page (statement status filter).
- Document the pattern so new pages follow it.
- Apply it to other filtered pages as a follow-up rather than all at once.

resultJson.description:
Make the bank statements list URL friendly (GitHub issue #81). Today the account selector and the "Filter by name" text field on `/bank-statements` are only `Hooks.useState` in `BankStatementList`. Refreshing the page, sharing the link, or coming back from a statement review resets the account to the default (the account with the newest upload). After this epic the URL holds that state (`/bank-statements?account=<accountKey>&q=<name>`). The list reads its filters from the URL and writes them back with `history.replace`, so filter changes don't add history entries and the browser Back button behaves sensibly. Pushing to a review and then pressing browser Back returns to the filtered list. The review page's in-app "← Back" button goes to the list with the statement's own account selected, and that also works when the review was opened cold in a new tab.

Note: the issue mentions a "statement status filter", but the page has no status filter. Its only filters are the account select and the filename text filter. Phase 1 covers those two. Do not invent a status filter. Other filtered pages are out of scope for now. The general rule goes into `docs/guide/frontend.md`, where it replaces the narrower existing RULE-FE-013 (which only covered pagination and allowed mount-only reads), so new pages follow it.

The issue also asks that deep links (`/bank-statements?account=…`, `/bank-statements/{id}`) resolve on a cold load, which overlaps with #80's ctrl+click bug. Reading the code did not reveal a client-side redirect that would explain landing on `/expenses`, so that task starts with investigating and reproducing the bug. Only the deep-link part of #80 is in scope here. #80's delete-confirmation dialog and stop-propagation fixes are not.

tasks.title: Bank statements list: account + name filters live in the URL
tasks.description:
Add pure URL helpers to `BankStatementsLogic` (web/.../pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsLogic.scala):
- `case class ListQuery(account: String, name: String)` ("" = absent)
- `def parseListQuery(search: String): ListQuery`, which reads `account` and `q` via `org.scalajs.dom.URLSearchParams` (null → "")
- `def listPath(account: Option[String], name: String): String`, which returns `/bank-statements` plus `?…` only for non-empty params, built with `URLSearchParams.set` + `toString` so spaces and special characters are encoded and round-trip through `parseListQuery`
- `def accountKey(bankName: String, productType: String, accountLast4: String): String`. Make `BankStatementList.accountKeyOf` delegate to it so the key format is defined in one place.

Wire `BankStatementList.component` (BankStatementsPage.scala) as follows:
- Get `val location = RouterCompat.useTypedLocation()`.
- Remove the `accountFilter` useState. Derive the chosen account from `parseListQuery(location.search).account` on every render, so browser back/forward within the route stays in sync. Keep passing it through `BankStatementsLogic.selectedAccountKey`, which keeps the existing fallback to the default account when the param is missing or stale.
- Keep the name filter as `Hooks.useState`, initialised from the URL `q`. Local state keeps the controlled TextField's cursor stable.
- Write on change with `history.replace(BankStatementsLogic.listPath(...))`. The account select writes the new key plus the current name. The name field sets state and writes the current URL account plus the new text.
- Use replace, not push, so filter tweaks don't add Back-button entries. Card clicks still `history.push` to the review, so browser Back from a review lands on the filtered list.

Tests: extend `BankStatementsLogicSpec` (pure, no DOM test):
- `parseListQuery` with empty, `?`, account only, both params, and URL-encoded values (a bank name with spaces, `~`)
- `listPath`: no params → `/bank-statements`; round-trip `parseListQuery(listPath(...).dropWhile(_ != '?'))`
- `accountKey` matches `accountKeyOf`

Verify with `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementsLogicSpec *BankStatementListSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Review page "← Back" returns to the list with the statement's account selected
tasks.description:
In `web/.../pages/bankstatementreview/BankStatementReviewHeader.scala`, the "← Back" button currently does `history.push("/bank-statements")`, which drops the filter. Change it to push `BankStatementsLogic.listPath(Some(BankStatementsLogic.accountKey(stmt.bankName, stmt.productType, stmt.accountLast4)), "")`. `GetBankStatement.Response` has these three fields. The list then opens on the reviewed statement's account even when the review was opened cold or in a new tab, with no dependency on browser history.

Don't use `history.goBack()`: it breaks on cold loads and new tabs. If the clean way to compute the path is a small pure function, extract it (for example `BankStatementReviewLogic.backToListPath(stmt)`, or reuse `BankStatementsLogic` directly) and unit-test it.

Tests: add a case to `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec` or `BankStatementsLogicSpec` asserting that the back path for a statement selects its account and round-trips through `parseListQuery`.

Verify with targeted `testOnly` plus `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Deep links to bank statement pages resolve on a cold load
tasks.description:
Goal: opening `/bank-statements?account=<key>&q=x` or `/bank-statements/<uuid>` in a fresh tab (ctrl/cmd+click uses `dom.window.open(reviewPath, "_blank")` in BankStatementsPage.scala) lands on that page with that state. #80 reports it landing on the expenses list.

Investigate first and reproduce before changing anything. The expenses list is only reached through AppRouter's `homeRedirect` (`/` → `/expenses`), so something sends the cold load to `/` first. Candidates:
- `catchAllRoute` (`Redirect("/")`) rendering while `$auth` is still `Unauthenticated`. `AppSplash` waits for `currentUser`, but check the ordering against `ReactiveHooks.useDistinctValue`'s initial `value()`.
- A route in the `Switch` order not matching.
- Server/infra fallback: nginx `try_files … /index.html`, webpack `historyApiFallback`, `<base href="/">` in web/src/main/js/index.html.
- The session cookie (application.conf `play.http.session.path`/domain) not being sent on the first request.

If the cause is client-side in web/, fix it cleanly (no setTimeout or flag hacks) and add a pure or minimal test that guards it. If you can only justify a DOM test, say in a comment which runtime failure it prevents (RULE-TE-010). If the cause is infra/server config or can't be reproduced, don't guess-patch. Report the findings and the exact proposed change instead.

Also confirm that the URL params from the list page survive a cold load, i.e. nothing strips the query string on redirect. Don't implement #80's delete confirmation or stopPropagation work.

tasks.title: Document the URL-friendly pages rule in the frontend guide
tasks.description:
Rewrite RULE-FE-013 in `docs/guide/frontend.md` as the general rule from #81: pages must be URL friendly. User-selected filters and view selections (account, search text, tab, page) go in the URL path or query params, not only in component state, so pages are refreshable, shareable and back-navigable.

Cover:
- Read the initial state from the URL (`RouterCompat.useTypedLocation().search` + `URLSearchParams`). Prefer deriving it on each render over a mount-only `useState` initialiser, so browser back/forward within the route stays in sync. Local state initialised from the URL is fine for free-text inputs.
- Write on change with `history.replace` for filters, search text and tab switches, and `history.push` only for changes the user expects Back to undo (moving to another page or record, pagination where that's wanted).
- Build and parse URLs in pure helpers (the example is `BankStatementsLogic.parseListQuery`/`listPath`) and unit-test them rather than writing DOM tests.
- Omit params that hold defaults, and fall back gracefully when a param is stale.
- "Back" buttons should build the target URL from the data they have, not depend on `history.goBack()`.

Update the `@file` references to live examples: `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsPage.scala` and `.../BankStatementsLogic.scala`, plus `.../bankstatementreview/BankStatementReviewContent.scala` (`?tab=` with replace). Fix the stale path: BulkMerchantSetupPage lives under `pages/merchants/`. Remove the bullet that calls mount-only reads "acceptable".

Optionally add a one-line entry to `docs/guide/antipatterns.md` §Frontend: "filter or view state held only in useState". Docs only, no code.

resultJson.brief:
Modules
- web/ is the Scala.js frontend: Slinky 0.7, React 18, MUI 5 through ScalablyTyped (`com.olvind.mui.muiMaterial.components as mui`), and a react-router v5 facade in `net.wiringbits.webapp.utils.slinkyUtils.facades.reactrouterdom` (`useHistory`, `useParams`, `useLocation`, `Route`, `Switch`, `Redirect`, `BrowserRouter`). `history.push(path: String)` and `history.replace(path: String)` take the same signature.
- Pages live in web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/<area>/. Tests live in web/src/test/scala/... (ScalaTest `AnyWordSpec`, `org.scalatest.matchers.must.Matchers.*`, jsdom env, so the global `URLSearchParams` is available).

Key files
- web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsPage.scala
  - `BankStatementsPage` fetches with `AsyncComponent` and renders `BankStatementList(ctx, stmts, onRefresh)`.
  - `BankStatementList.component` holds `stmtFilter` (name text, `Hooks.useState("")`) and `accountFilter` (`Hooks.useState("")`, where \"\" = not chosen). It computes `accounts`, `selectedAccount = BankStatementsLogic.selectedAccountKey(accountFilter, localStmts)` and `timeline = BankStatementsLogic.timeline(localStmts, selectedAccount, stmtFilter)`.
  - Filters are rendered at roughly lines 424-448: an MUI select TextField labelled \"Account\" and a \"Filter by name\" TextField.
  - Card click: `history.push(s\"/bank-statements/${s.id}\")`, or `dom.window.open(reviewPath, \"_blank\")` on ctrl/meta.
  - Helpers: `BankStatementList.accountKeyOf(s) = s\"${s.bankName}~${s.productType}~${s.accountLast4}\"`, plus `accountLabelOf`, `metadataLine`, `gapWarning`.
- web/.../pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsLogic.scala holds the pure logic (no React/MUI): `defaultAccountKey(stmts): Option[String]`, `selectedAccountKey(chosen: String, stmts): Option[String]` (keeps chosen if it still exists, else the default) and `timeline(stmts, accountKey: Option[String], nameFilter: String)`. Tests: web/src/test/.../bankstatements/BankStatementsLogicSpec.scala and BankStatementListSpec.scala (both pure, with a `stmt(...)` builder).
- web/.../pages/bankstatementreview/BankStatementReviewHeader.scala: the \"← Back\" button does `history.push(\"/bank-statements\")`. Props has `statement: GetBankStatement.Response` (fields include id, bankName, productType, accountLast4, currency, periodStart/End).
- web/.../pages/bankstatementreview/BankStatementReviewContent.scala is an existing URL-state example: it reads `?tab=` with `new URLSearchParams(location.search)` and writes with `history.replace(s\"$pathname?tab=$tab\")`.
- web/.../pages/merchants/BulkMerchantSetupPage.scala is another example (`?page=`, push).
- web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/webapp/utils/slinkyUtils/compat/RouterCompat.scala has `RouterCompat.useTypedLocation(): Location(pathname: String, search: String)`. This is the only approved way to read the location. `js.Dynamic`/`asInstanceOf` are banned outside compat/ (RULE-FE-014).
- web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/AppRouter.scala
  - Authenticated `Switch` order: `/` → `Redirect(\"/expenses\")`, …, `/bank-statements/bulk-expenses`, `/bank-statements/bulk-setup`, `/bank-statements/:stmtId/auto-reconcile`, `/bank-statements/:stmtId`, `/bank-statements/import/:draftId`, `/bank-statements`, …, and `catchAllRoute = Route(path=\"*\")(render = Redirect(\"/\"))`. All routes use exact=true.
  - App.scala wraps it in `BrowserRouter(basename=\"\")` inside `AppSplash`. AppSplash.scala calls `api.client.currentUser`, then `ctx.loggedIn(user)` (`$auth := Authenticated`), then `setInitialized(true)`, and renders children only after that.
  - `ReactiveHooks.useDistinctValue` seeds state with `value()`.
  - `Main.scala` starts `$auth` as `Unauthenticated`.
- Infra and serving: web/src/main/js/index.html has `<base href=\"/\">` and a relative bundle src. custom.webpack.config.js has `historyApiFallback: true`. infra/config/nginx/web_app_site.j2 has `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html`. server application.conf sets the session cookie `__APP_SESSION__` with path `${play.http.context}`.
- docs/guide/frontend.md: RULE-FE-013 currently covers \"Persist pageable/filterable state in the URL\" (pagination-centric). Its @file path for BulkMerchantSetupPage is stale (the page is now under pages/merchants/). docs/guide/testing.md RULE-TE-010 says to prefer pure-function unit tests over DOM tests, and any DOM test must justify the runtime failure it guards.

Conventions
- Component shape (RULE-FE-001): `object X { def apply(...): KeyAddingStage; case class Props; val component = FunctionalComponent[Props] {...} }`.
- Hook deps go through `SafeHooks.useEffect(key: String)` / `useMemo`, with String keys only (RULE-FE-006).
- Put pure logic in `*Logic` objects and unit-test it.
- No hacks: no setTimeout for ordering, no ad-hoc flags. If there's no clean fix, stop and report.
- Name same-typed arguments at call sites (for example `listPath(account = ..., name = ...)`).
- `scalajs-dom` `URLSearchParams` supports `new URLSearchParams(init: String)`, `.get(k)` (returns null when absent), `.set(k, v)` and `.toString()`. It encodes spaces as `+`, which `get` decodes.
- Account keys look like `BBVA~credit~1234` and bank names may contain spaces.

Build and test
- Targeted only: `sbt \"web/testOnly *BankStatementsLogicSpec\"` (and others as needed) or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. Don't run the full `sbt test`.
- Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default shell node is v16, and yarn install fails with it).
- Run scalafmt (`sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`) before finishing.

resultJson.title: Keep bank statement list filters in the URL
resultJson.body:
Implements phase 1 of #81. The bank statements list now keeps its filters in the URL as `/bank-statements?account=<key>&q=<name>`, so a refresh or a shared link opens the same view.

- **List page:** the selected account is read from the URL on every render. The name filter uses local state that starts from the URL and re-syncs when the URL changes. Filter changes use `history.replace`, so they don't add Back-button entries. Opening a statement still uses `push`, so browser Back returns to the filtered list. A missing or stale `account` still falls back to the default account.
- **Review page "← Back":** builds the list URL from the statement's own account (`BankStatementReviewLogic.backToListPath`) instead of using `history.goBack()`. This works even when the review was opened in a new tab.
- **Helpers:** `BankStatementsLogic` now has `parseListQuery`, `listPath` and `accountKey`, with unit tests. The query parsing is hand-written on top of `URIUtils` because the jsdom used in tests doesn't provide `URLSearchParams`.
- **Docs:** RULE-FE-013 in `docs/guide/frontend.md` is rewritten as the general "pages must be URL friendly" rule, and the stale `BulkMerchantSetupPage` path is fixed. Anti-pattern AP-FE-09 is added.

Notes for reviewers:
- The issue mentions a status filter, but the page doesn't have one. The only filters are the account select and the name text field, so this PR covers just those two.
- This diff has no code change for the cold-load deep-link item that overlaps with #80.
- Other filtered pages are left for a follow-up.

Closes #81
